newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares nudge up at close, Reliance rallies.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares nudge up at close, Reliance rallies.

text.p: Share prices inched up at close on Thursday at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) behind a strong surge in Reliance stock, brokers said.
Reliance jumped 6.0 rupees to 194.75 in volume of over 3.2 million shares ahead of the petrochemical giant's results for the six months to September 30.
Analysts forecast Reliance's net profit to fall 25 percent in the first half due to poor market conditions, but traders say the firm was likely to overcome the shortfall from higher "other income".
"That Reliance's profits will be hit is no news," said trader Ramnik Parikh. "The matter to note is there could be a pleasant surprise."
Reliance is scheduled to unveil the results on Friday.
The share gained 5.65 rupees to 194.05 in volume of more than 10 million shares at the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Traders said selective purchases by state-run domestic investment institutions also helped the market recover from an early slide.
Insurance firms and the Unit Trust of India, the country's largest mutual fund, were buyers, the traders said.
The market was oversold after a four-month long slide but recovery was limited due to delays in policy implementation and ahead of first half company results, Kotak Securities said.

The 30-share BSE index ended 5.37 points, or 0.17 percent, higher at 3,110.03 after hitting 3,068.56. The 50-stock NSE finished 1.0 points, or 0.11 percent, lower at 892.0. Both closings were provisional.
SBI gained 1.50 rupees to 210, TISCO 2.0 to 172.50 and BSES 2.75 to 175, while Bajaj Auto shed 4.25 to 926.50 and ACC 18.50 to 1,628.75.
